title: Preparation of phase change material filled hybrid 2D/3D graphene structure with ultra-high thermal effusivity for effective thermal management
author: Liang, Zhang, et al.

steps.title: Cast GO paper on copper
steps.instruction: Prepare an 8 mg ml⁻¹ graphene‑oxide (GO) aqueous solution, then cast it onto a copper foil using a blade; adjust the blade speed and the gap between blade and foil to obtain the desired paper thickness.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 8 mg ml⁻¹ GO aqueous solution.
Cast the solution onto copper foil with a moving blade.
Control paper thickness by varying blade speed and blade‑to‑foil distance.

steps.title: Two‑step anneal to graphene paper
steps.instruction: Thermally anneal the GO paper in two stages: first at 1100 °C to reduce it to reduced graphene oxide (rGO) paper, then at 2600 °C to graphitize it into graphene paper (GP).

substeps.instruction: Anneal GO paper at 1100 °C to obtain rGO paper.
Anneal rGO paper at 2600 °C to obtain GP.

steps.title: Press graphene paper
steps.instruction: Compress the freshly formed graphene paper at 20 MPa for 5 minutes to increase its density and thermal conductivity.

steps.title: Vacuum impregnate PU foam with GO
steps.instruction: Place a polyurethane (PU) foam template in a vacuum chamber and repeatedly impregnate it with the same 8 mg ml⁻¹ GO aqueous solution until fully saturated.

substeps.instruction: Insert PU foam into vacuum chamber.
Introduce GO solution and apply vacuum.
Repeat impregnation cycles to ensure complete saturation.

steps.title: Two‑step anneal to graphene foam
steps.instruction: Thermally treat the GO‑loaded PU foam using the same two‑step schedule (1100 °C then 2600 °C) to simultaneously remove the PU template and convert the GO into a three‑dimensional graphene foam (GF).

substeps.instruction: Anneal at 1100 °C to decompose PU and reduce GO.
Anneal at 2600 °C to graphitize the reduced GO into GF.

steps.title: Vacuum impregnate graphene foam with SA
steps.instruction: Under vacuum, fully infiltrate the resulting graphene foam with stearic acid (SA) to produce the stearic‑acid‑filled graphene‑foam composite (GFSAC).

substeps.instruction: Place GF in a vacuum chamber.
Introduce SA (solid or melt) and maintain vacuum to allow complete impregnation.

steps.title: Assemble and melt SA to form sandwich
steps.instruction: Place a piece of graphene paper at the bottom of the GFSAC, then heat the assembly under vacuum to the melting point of SA; the molten SA will flow downward, wet the GP (wetting angle ≈70.06°) and fill the gap by capillary action, yielding the GP/GFSAC/GP composite.

substeps.instruction: Position GP at the bottom of the GFSAC block.
Heat under vacuum until SA melts (reach SA melting point).
Allow molten SA to flow, wetting GP and filling the interfacial gap.
